definitions: A family unit in which several generations of a family live together in the same household, often including parents, their children, and their children's spouses and offspring.
An extended family arrangement common in some cultures, where multiple nuclear families related by blood or marriage reside together and share resources and responsibilities.
examples: In many traditional societies, the joint family was the norm.
Living in a joint family can offer strong social support.
The property was managed by the head of the joint family.
